subject: Re: Demo time — aligning US/EU daylight-savings boundary
messages:
From: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@heliobank.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: Tomás Álvarez <tomas.alvarez@heliobank.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0400
Subject: Request to shift Friday demo (US/EU DST mismatch week)

Hi Rachel —

Quick heads-up: our EU offices will switch to DST this Sunday while the US switches two weeks later. The team in Madrid (Tomás and I) noticed the demo scheduled for Friday at 11:00 AM ET will fall into that mismatch window, which makes it awkward for our APAC colleagues and for local calendars.

Can we move the demo to one of these options?
- Friday 9:30 AM ET / 15:30 CET (earlier for US, within working hours in EU)
- Friday 3:00 PM ET / 21:00 CET (late for EU, OK for US)

We'd prefer the earlier slot if it keeps APAC from having to join after hours. Also, please resend the calendar invite so the timezone anchor is explicit (we've had double-booking problems when invites use floating times).

Thanks —
Sophie
Sophie Lambert
Director of Platform Integrations, HelioBank
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@heliobank.com>
Cc: Tomás Álvarez <tomas.alvarez@heliobank.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 08 Apr 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request to shift Friday demo (US/EU DST mismatch week)

Hi Sophie —

Thanks for the heads-up, really glad you flagged the DST boundary. Agree we should anchor the invite to a single timezone to avoid floating times. Quick notes from our side:

- We prefer the earlier option (9:30 AM ET / 15:30 CET) to keep APAC less impacted.
- I'll include an explicit timezone annotation in the invite (ET) and add an alternate time field in the description for clarity.
- Attaching a timezone matrix and our proposed agenda — please confirm the attendees for the hands-on portion so we can split the walkthrough into two short segments.

Proposed next steps:
1) Sophie confirms the 9:30 AM ET option by EOD Thursday.
2) I send an updated calendar invite anchored to ET with both CET and IST conversions in the body.
3) Vivek will prepare a short section on performance/latency differences between hosted and dedicated modes for European deployments.

If that works, I'll update the invite and push both files to the calendar.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood_demo_agenda.pdf, timezone_matrix.xlsx
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>, Sophie Lambert <sophie.lambert@heliobank.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Tomás Álvarez <tomas.alvarez@heliobank.com>
Date: Thu, 09 Apr 2026 08:27:00 +01:00
Subject: Re: Request to shift Friday demo (US/EU DST mismatch week)

Thanks Rachel —

Confirming I'll take the latency section. A couple of practical requests that will help during the live demo: 

- Can HelioBank provide the expected peak QPS for the demo data (even a rough number)? We'll pre-warm caches accordingly.
- For the recording, please confirm if we should mute any environment-specific hostnames — security prefers to scrub internal hostnames before sharing externally.

Also: if we anchor the invite to ET, please include the explicit UTC conversion line (UTC-4 during US pre-switch; UTC+2 for CET after EU switch). That will make the changeover transparent for everyone.

Cheers,
Vivek
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Rachel/Vivek —

Confirmed: the team prefers Friday 9:30 AM ET / 15:30 CET. Peak QPS for our test dataset will be ~120 QPS (burst to 250). We'd like the session recorded and shared with the broader infra team; please keep hostnames redacted in the public recording.

Thanks for moving fast on this — we'll look out for the updated invite.
